checks: The cyclic descent action is q0 times inverse geometric deck pullback after trivializing the coefficient sheaf on the actual field-kernel cover. The geometric deck automorphism is k-linear; the field multiplier is not silently treated as geometric Frobenius on roots of unity.

Minimal-resolution uniqueness gives a coherent deck action also whenp dividesa. The existing genus and component budgets apply on a degree-ta cover. Regular input can be replaced by the single invariant closed-point blowup. Blowing all non-SNC points at each stage is an invariant sequence of disjoint centres, and the previously proved finite-prefix2delta+7G bound introduces no extra factor a.

The full SNC support/Picard sequences are natural for regular-pair isomorphisms. They give the stated equivariant filtration by coker(N mod n), component Jacobian torsion and integral graph homology; no equivariant splitting or invariant spanning tree is assumed.

For the quotientQ_n the kernel-cokernel sequence really costs two permutation factors: coker(u onI_n) has the same order as ker(u onI_n), which injects into ker(u onP_n). Thus ker(u onQ_n)<=ker(u onP_n)^2. This check is necessary; left exactness on quotients alone would be false.

Smith normal form bounds every lattice kernel modulo n by the characteristic-zero determinant. Finite-order deck eigenvalues are roots of unity. On the product Jacobian, (q0-tau) times its geometric sum is[n], making it an isogeny; the degree/Tate-characteristic-polynomial theorem gives the2sumg exponent even for wild deck order.

The degree-one localization sequence is obtained after removing the invariant finite node set, by codimension-two then divisor purity. Its final image is a subgroup of the exceptional permutation module. The normalization sequence gives the graph/Jacobian filtration, and finite kernel/cokernel equality yields the stated H1(V) cokernel bound.

The cyclic coefficient norm has image precisely theF_q0* invariant subgroup, so H2(C_a,M)=0. The (1,1) Cartan-Leray term embeds into the H1(V) cokernel, and the (0,2) term is the independently bounded H2(V) invariant kernel. Possible differentials only pass to subquotients; the argument never claims degeneration.
The total exponent is2v+2sumg+b1+v+2pg <=3v+4pg. Sincepg+v=O_R(ta),q0+1<=q0² andq0^a=q, the result is q^(c_Rt) with no remaining field-cover factor.

For the nonconstant finite sheaf, pass to a cover where it becomes constant; every degree-one torsor dies after a further finite etale cover and Galois closure. The universal-cover five-term sequence gives the group-to-scheme H2 injection without any tameness hypothesis.
The period in the final remark is measured only after restriction to the field-kernel cover, where the band is constant. No ordinaryG_m Brauer image of the nonconstant band onU_H is asserted.
